answer: For standard reimbursement claims, you have 30 days from the date of discharge to submit the claim [1][2]. However, for Aurora Group Health corporate plans, the submission window is 60 days from discharge [5]. (Archived 2024 rules listed the deadline as 15 days [3].)
The room rent limit on the Silver plan is 2% of the sum insured per day [3][4].
No, maternity is not covered on the Bronze plan at any sum insured [1][2].

The waiting period for pre-existing diseases is 36 months on standard retail plans, which applies to conditions such as hypertension, diabetes, and cardiac conditions unless explicitly waived in writing [3][5]. Under the Aurora Senior Care plan for ages 60 and above, the waiting period for pre-existing diseases is reduced to 24 months [5].
The grace period for an annual policy is 30 days from the renewal due date [1][5].
Aurora's network covers 11,400 hospitals across 780 towns as of 1 April 2026 [1].

Under the Aurora Gold plan, the no-claim bonus is 25% of the base sum insured per claim-free year, accumulating up to a maximum of 100% [1][5]. If a claim is made, the bonus is not reduced; it simply stops accumulating for that year [1].
No, you cannot claim for IVF treatment because it is listed under permanent exclusions [1].
Under the Aurora Gold plan, the sub-limit for cataract surgery is ₹75,000 per eye [1].

If you are not satisfied with the Stage 1 outcome, you can escalate the matter to Aurora's Grievance Redressal Officer [2]. If Aurora's final response remains unsatisfactory (or if there is no response within 30 days of the original complaint), you may approach the Insurance Ombudsman for your region [1].

All plans include road ambulance cover of ₹5,000 per hospitalisation [1]. Additionally, the Aurora Gold plan provides air ambulance cover up to ₹2,50,000 per policy year within India on prior authorisation [5].
Yes, in-patient treatment for mental illness is covered on the same terms as physical illness [1]. The standard 30-day initial waiting period applies, with no separate waiting period required [1].

The free-look period is the window in which a new policy can be returned for a refund [3]. A new policyholder may cancel within 15 days of receiving the policy document, or 30 days if the policy was sold through distance marketing [1][2]. Upon cancellation, the policyholder receives a premium refund minus the proportionate risk premium for the period of cover, medical examination costs, and stamp duty [2].
You receive 150 wellness points for completing an annual health check-up [1].

A day-care procedure is a procedure that requires less than 24 hours of hospitalisation because of technological advance, making it payable despite the general 24-hour admission requirement [3]. Out-patient treatment is not considered a day-care procedure [3].
For a cashless emergency admission, the hospital must notify Aurora within 24 hours of admission [1][5].
No, Aurora administers its own claims and does not use a TPA [1].
To qualify as a hospital under the policy, a facility must have at least 10 in-patient beds in towns with a population below 10 lakh, or at least 15 in-patient beds elsewhere [1].

No, everything will not be paid [5]. On a ₹5,00,000 Silver plan, the room-rent limit is 2% (₹10,000 per day), meaning occupying a room at ₹15,000 per day triggers an eligibility ratio of 0.667 (10,000 ÷ 15,000) [1]. Because of proportionate deductions, associated medical charges will be reduced and paid only up to that proportion, leaving a portion of the bill to be paid out-of-pocket [1][5].

Dependent parents can be added under the Silver plan (at an extra premium), Gold plan, and Platinum plan, but they cannot be covered under the Bronze plan [1]. When a parent is added, the policy premium is recalculated based on the age of the eldest member covered, which often costs more than purchasing a separate individual senior-citizen policy for that parent [4].

The waiting period you have already served will carry over, but only up to the sum insured of your previous policy, including any accrued no-claim bonus [1][2]. Any increase or incremental amount in the sum insured will be subject to fresh waiting periods [1][2].

You must inform Aurora within 90 days of birth to add your newborn to the policy as a dependent so that coverage continues beyond the initial 90 days without medical underwriting [1]. If you need to submit a reimbursement claim for the hospitalisation, you must file it within 30 days of discharge and submit post-hospitalisation bills within 15 days of the applicable period ending [3].
The out-patient benefit (OPD rider) is not available on the Bronze plan [1]. However, the provided sources do not specifically mention coverage or reimbursement rules for physiotherapy sessions.
Under the Aurora Silver plan, a claim reduces your accumulated no-claim bonus by 10 percentage points, rather than resetting it to zero [1].
Under the Gold plan, the coverage limit for a Caesarean section is ₹1,00,000 per delivery [1]. If the hospital bills ₹1,60,000, your out-of-pocket cost would be ₹60,000 [1].

Knee replacement is not covered immediately if it is unrelated to an accident, as it is subject to a 24-month waiting period [1][5]. However, if the knee replacement is needed following an accidental injury, it is covered immediately from day one with no waiting period [1][2][5].
Total discounts are capped at 30% of the base premium [1]. The wellness discount (up to 15%) is applied last, after the cap, and is the only discount that may exceed the 30% limit [1][3][5].

Cashless access is not available at an excluded provider and will be denied [2][3]. Instead, you must file for reimbursement, which is only payable if the admission was a genuine emergency with no reachable alternative facility [1], and pre-approval is required [3]. Denial of cashless is not a rejection of the claim itself [4].

The deadline to respond to an Aurora query depends on the claim type:
* For general reimbursement claims, you have 45 days from the date of the query to respond [2][5].
* For motor insurance claims, the deadline is 30 days from the date of the query [4].

The sources disagree on the notification timeline for a planned cashless admission. One source states that notification must be made 48 hours before admission [1], while other sources state it must be at least 72 hours before admission [2][3].

Aurora settles or rejects a complete reimbursement claim within 15 working days of receiving the last required document [1][2]. If Aurora raises a query, the clock restarts once the queried document is supplied [1]. (Archived 2024 rules previously allowed 30 days from the last document [3].)
Aurora Gold has no co-payment at any age [1]. Additionally, Aurora Silver has no co-payment for insured members below age 60 [2].

Across the four plans, the pre-hospitalisation coverage windows are 30 days, 45 days, 60 days, and 90 days [1]. The corresponding post-hospitalisation coverage windows are 60 days, 90 days, 120 days, and 180 days [1].

You should consider the Gold plan, as it removes room-rent sub-limits [3] and covers dependent parents-in-law [1]. The Platinum plan also covers dependent parents-in-law [1], though specific room-rent details for Platinum are not fully provided in the excerpts.

Out-patient dental work is not covered by any plan [1]. Furthermore, dental treatment and oral surgery are permanently excluded unless necessitated by an accidental injury requiring hospitalisation [2][3].
